findings.title: Switching task tabs silently discards unsaved queue and goal drafts

relatedLocations.reason: Queue edits exist only in the QueuePanel-owned ref map.
Goal editing flag, objective, budget selection and value exist only in GoalPanel state.
Tab controls switch unconditionally without preserving dirty state or warning.

trigger: Open Task Workflow, edit an existing queued message and type unsaved text; click Goal/Budget or Agents, then return to Queue.
Open Goal/Budget, begin creating or editing a goal, change objective and/or token budget without saving; visit another task tab, then return.
findings.consequence: The conditional branch unmounts the draft owner. Returning creates a fresh map/state and shows server values, losing unsaved instructions and/or budget without an explicit discard action or warning. Switching tabs while a submitted edit awaits a result also destroys the draft-owning component.
findings.evidence: React component state/ref lifetime plus full source trace; no test executed. Existing workflows tests cover pending edit locks/failure retention (line 231), sibling/failed/missing refresh preservation (lines 331 and 364), and owner change isolation (line 408). No test clicks away from an unsaved task editor and back to assert preservation within the same thread and epoch.
findings.recommendation: Lazily mount task panels on first visit and retain them under hidden containers for the same owner, or lift queue and goal draft state above the conditional tab boundary. Preserve owner isolation, pending-operation locks, size bounds and explicit discard behavior; tab changes must not submit mutations. Add interaction regressions for queue text and goal objective/budget surviving tab round trips, pending/rejected edit round trips and owner changes.
findings.ownerBoundary: Workspace.tsx:1440-1443 already keys TaskPanel by threadId plus resourceEpoch. Therefore this report does not claim cross-thread goal-state leakage at the current application entrypoint merely because GoalPanel lacks its own key.

delegation.note: Root authorized splitting the original 193-file assignment. This reviewer completed the 131-file sub-scope; root must union its coverage with the independent 65-test report to establish all 193 web files are covered.

limitations: No dynamic confirmation of the finding; it follows directly from current React unmount semantics.
CSS was statically inspected; actual browser layout, OS IME, accessibility tree and live streaming integrations were not exercised.
scopeReassignment: Root explicitly reassigned this reviewer to the complete 128 non-test web files plus 3 actually reviewed tests; public_r4_runtime independently owns all 65 web test/support files. complete=true refers only to these 131 inspectedFiles, not a claim of single-reviewer coverage of the original 193 files.
